text:
Bleedin' Blue made the case on Nov. 2 that Pavel Buchnevich has become one of the Blues' most important players. The points don't show it yet. He has 7 in 16 games, and just 2 in his last ten, both goals, against 5.8 our numbers expected from his ice time.

The underlying play is better than the line. St. Louis takes 52.8% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on the ice, 5.6 points better than without him, and his chances, 0.82 expected goals per 60, match last season. He has 3 goals on 3.9 expected, so his finishing is close to normal. What's missing is the assists, the part that depends on teammates finishing.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking gives him a signature worth watching: 19% of his setups come from behind the net, against 8% for a typical forward. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, so the case for him rests on this year's play. St. Louis has lost three of its last four. A few of his passes going in would help both.
headline: Buchnevich's points have gone quiet
